chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Fatty Arbuckle and Webb in the back of the saloon
summary: Spikes played three or four weeks for Arbuckle and his Dutch-comedian partner Webb around 1909, before Arbuckle was in the movies.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And that was... It was during that period that you played for Fatty Arbuckle. Is that right?
Was he just starting out then?
Yeah, they were just starting--he and a fella named Webb, I think. Fatty was Irish, and the other guy was a Dutch
comedian--Irish and Dutch comedian. Yeah, they worked in the back of the saloon, and we played for them.
Do you think they were funny?
Yeah! They were funny. Fatty's always funny to me.
And how long did you work with him there?
Oh, I guess three or four weeks. That's about as long as you work in...
How much later than that was it that he went to Hollywood? Do you know? I don't know.
Dunno, that was about 1909, and I fooled around back in show business, and then I come here and come home to stay and uh, you know, '17 or '18, and he was up in the movies then, you know. Yeah.
